newsitem.title: TURKEY: Israel's Levy upbeat on Turkish ties.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy upbeat on Turkish ties.

text.p: Israel's Foreign Minister David Levy started a potentially contentious visit to Turkey on Tuesday, saying a majority in the overwhelmingly-Moslem country supported expanded ties to the Jewish state.
"Growing relations between the two countries are supported by the majority of (our) two countries," Levy said at Ankara airport before heading for a series of talks with Turkish leaders.
"The ratification of the free trade agreement between Turkey and Israel is proof of that," he said. Turkish MPs backed the measures late last week, with support from the ruling Islamists.

Levy's two-day visit includes a meeting later on Tuesday with Islamist Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan, a long-standing critic of Israel and a bitter opponent of growing military and commercial ties.

That meeting, however, was in doubt as late as Monday afternoon, when Erbakan finally agreed to see the Israeli envoy. The delay provoked an angry outburst from the Israeli embassy in Ankara, frustrated by the prime minister's late reply.
Nevertheless, Levy made it clear he hoped to smooth relations with Erbakan, modern Turkey's first Islamist leader.
"His stance will be heard. He will also hear our stance," he said before leaving Israel for the short flight to Ankara.
Levy will also meet Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller of the coalition's secularist wing and President Suleyman Demirel. He meets Jewish leaders in Istanbul on Wednesday.
